headline: Consumers Worldwide Pay $468 Billion Due to Iran War Fuel Price Surge
summary: Consumers worldwide paid an additional $468 billion for petrol and diesel due to supply disruptions resulting from the U.S. war on Iran.
why: Energy price spikes directly drive consumer inflation and elevate operational costs across global transport and manufacturing sectors.

impacts.name: Energy
impacts.why: Supply disruptions from the war on Iran drove up global petrol and diesel prices.

why_moved: Global fuel price surges increase input costs for businesses and consumers worldwide, impacting broader inflation expectations.
